previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of liver transplant for primary sclerosing cholangitis was admitted with a month-long history of fever, headaches, nausea, and abdominal pain. She was found to have severe neutropenia, likely due to medication effects from MMF and dapsone, with an initial concern for CMV viremia. Repeat testing showed undetectable CMV viral load, ruling out active infection. Dapsone was switched to atovaquone, MMF was temporarily held, and Neupogen was administered to support white blood cell recovery. A colonoscopy was performed due to concern for colitis, revealing a normal colon with negative biopsies for CMV. Her white count improved, and she remained afebrile. She was discharged home with resolved symptoms, resumed immunosuppression, and plans for outpatient follow-up including repeat colonoscopy for screening.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman s/p liver transplant who 
presented with dizziness, which she described as an unsteady 
feeling, a feeling of falling, and a feeling such as being on a 
ship. This sensation has been present more prominent since the 
beginning of ___ and coincided with a medication change to 
Atovaquone. 

MRI showed no signs of acute stroke which was one of the 
concerns that prompted her admission. It was thought that the 
most likely explanation of her dizziness was a medication 
side-effect, given that her ataxia seems to be that of a 
cerebellar midline dysfunction -- she does not have appendicular 
ataxia of her arms, although her legs do show some ataxia. 
Overall it is more of a truncal ataxia. She also was quite 
nauseous with her dizziness. Her nausea was controlled with 
Zofran. She was evaluated by the physical therapists, who 
recommended outpatient vestibular therapy. 

Atovaquone can indeed cause dizziness, and while Ms. ___ 
endorses dizziness as a problem ever since her liver transplant, 
her dizziness worsened severely in the last 3 weeks, which 
coincides with the start of atovaquone.
After discussion with the liver team, we agreed to replace her 
atovaquone with Dapsone for antibiotic ppx. She has follow-up 
appointments in place with hepatology and neurology, to ensure 
that she is able to tolerate this medication change.

Ms. ___ agreed with plans for discharge and follow-up.

Post-hospital follow-up:
- Switched antibiotic ppx from atovaquone to dapsone. Please 
follow-up WBC in 1 week to make sure no dropping WBC while on 
Dapsone (this has happened in the past).
- Vestibular therapy for vertigo.
- Continue to follow tacro levels, though her initial level here 
was 9.2, it dropped down to 5.5 on the day of discharge, so not 
likely that a high tacro level caused her dizziness.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  CT HEAD W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  History: ___ with headache and vertigo// Evaluate for acute
bleed, with focus on posterior circulation

TECHNIQUE:  Routine unenhanced head CT was performed and viewed in brain,
intermediate and bone windows.  Coronal and sagittal reformats were also
performed.

DOSE:   Acquisition sequence:
   1) Sequenced Acquisition 16.0 s, 16.7 cm; CTDIvol = 48.0 mGy (Head) DLP =
802.7 mGy-cm.
 Total DLP (Head) = 803 mGy-cm.

COMPARISON:  MRI head ___
CT head ___

FINDINGS: 

There is no intra-axial or extra-axial hemorrhage, edema, shift of normally
midline structures, or evidence of acute major vascular territorial
infarction.  Ventricles and sulci are age appropriate.  Right lateral
ventricle is larger than the left, unchanged in appearance from CT head ___, likely representing congenital or developmental etiology.  Mild
atherosclerotic calcifications of the cavernous carotid arteries are
demonstrated.

There is mild mucosal thickening of the bilateral ethmoid air cells and right
sphenoid sinus.  Mastoid air cells and middle ear cavities are well aerated.
The bony calvarium is intact.

IMPRESSION: 

No intracranial hemorrhage or other acute intracranial abnormality.

EXAMINATION:  MRI AND MRA BRAIN AND MRA NECK PT11 MR ___

INDICATION:  Acute onset dizziness and headache.  Evaluate for infarct,
vascular stenosis, or cerebral venous thrombosis.

TECHNIQUE:  Three dimensional time of flight MR arteriography was performed
through the brain with maximum intensity projection reconstructions.

2D time of flight MR angiography of the neck was performed.

Brain imaging was performed with sagittal T1 and axial FLAIR, T2, gradient
echo and diffusion technique.

Three dimensional maximum intensity projection and segmented images were
generated. This report is based on interpretation of all of these images. The
examination was performed using a 1.5T MRI.

3D phase-contrast MRV of the head was obtained. Sagittal T1 weighted imaging
was performed. Three dimensional maximum intensity projection and segmented
images of the MRV were then generated. This report is based on interpretation
of all of these images.

COMPARISON:  Noncontrast head CT ___.  MR head ___.

FINDINGS: 

MRI Brain: There is no evidence of hemorrhage, edema, masses, mass effect,
midline shift or infarction.   The ventricles and sulci are within normal
limits in caliber and configuration for age.  Slight asymmetry of the lateral
ventricles is unchanged, likely developmental.  There is no abnormal focus of
slowed diffusion.

 The visualized paranasal sinuses are grossly clear.  The orbits are grossly
unremarkable.  The mastoid air cells are clear.

MRA brain: There is normal variant fetal type origin of the left PCA.  There
is mild irregularity of the bilateral intracranial internal carotid arteries
suggestive of atherosclerotic disease without significant narrowing.  The
intracranial vertebral and internal carotid arteries and their major branches
are otherwise patent without evidence of significant stenosis, occlusion, or
aneurysm formation.

MRV head: Normal flow signal is demonstrated within the superior sagittal
sinus, straight sinus, transverse sinuses, and sigmoid sinuses. The jugular
bulbs and proximal jugular veins are patent. Evaluation of the deep venous
systems reveals normal flow signal in the internal cerebral veins. The vein of
___ is also unremarkable.

MRA neck: There is minimal irregularity of the bilateral carotid bifurcations
suggesting atherosclerotic disease without significant narrowing.  The common,
internal and external carotid arteries appear patent.  There is no evidence of
internal carotid artery stenosis by NASCET criteria.  The origins of the great
vessels, subclavian and vertebral arteries appear patent bilaterally.

IMPRESSION:


1. No hemorrhage, infarct, or suggestion of mass.
2.  Patent intracranial arterial vasculature without significant stenosis,
occlusion, or aneurysm.
3.  Patent cervical arterial vasculature without significant stenosis, or
occlusion.
4. No evidence of cerebral venous thrombosis.
